analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | off cycle EPS | TEX
key_insights: US S&P futures are down 40bps pre-market after a broad rally the prior day. Asia followed the US higher with Taiwan up nearly 9%, KOSPI up 632bps and Japan up 391bps, while China lagged and Europe is lower led by Germany down 85bps.

Copper fell 400bps to $5.40. Brent is below $90 and WTI is approaching $80, at local lows, which the note reads as some relief in the choke point around the Strait. Many are calling for a medium-term oil surplus.
The 10-year yield is lower with treasuries bid at 4.9%, DXY holds at $104 and Bitcoin is risk off below $60k.
Privo on Risk says energy and rate impulses are supportive, and Williams sounded more balanced than Waller or Logan. Price action is described as bear market like, too violent for anyone to hold.

Privo says the best outcome now is for the market to sit still for a couple of days, letting excess vol premium bleed out and giving systematics room to re-lever. Year-end seasonals and a reprieve on oil or AI add potential demand, and shorts are still underwater.

TEX agreed to sell its Genie Access Work Platforms business to Linamar for $1.4bn at about 12x EV/EBITDA. Linamar expects $135mm of run-rate synergies. The deal is dilutive to TEX but frees capital and removes its most volatile, cyclical business.
BA headline: China Southern is buying 50 737-8 aircraft at a list price of $7.4bn, following a POTUS comment on further China orders.

TITN reported better Q3 EPS on topline and gross margins. Fiscal January 2027 guidance: agriculture down 10-15% (was down 15-20%), construction up 2.5-7.5% (was up 5-10%), Europe at the lower end of its prior guide, and Australia better.
AMTM Q4 revenue missed consensus while EBITDA was slightly ahead. FY27 EPS guide midpoint is a touch below consensus. A $500mm buyback was announced and the options market implies a 12% move.
J beat on Q4 EPS, EBITDA and backlog (up 24% YoY). FY27 EPS guide midpoint is roughly in line with consensus and revenue guide is above it. The options market implies an 8% move.
SYM beat Q4 EBITDA and guided Q1 EBITDA above consensus on slightly lower revenue. It highlighted an expanded WMT agreement, and the options market implies a 15% move.
GS Industrials and Materials Conference runs 12/2-12/3 with about 100 corporates. A preview is due this weekend. Watch IFO, Dell, Workday, the 5yr auction and consumer confidence today.

China Southern is reported to be purchasing 50 737-8 jets at a $7.4bn list price, following POTUS comments on further China orders.
Better Q3 EPS and a raised agriculture outlook, offset by a lower construction guide.
Q4 revenue missed consensus and FY27 EPS guide midpoint is slightly below, partly offset by a $500mm buyback.

earnings_insights: AMTM Q4 reported 11/23: EPS $0.71 vs consensus est $0.66, revenue $3.62bn vs consensus est $3.7bn, EBITDA $304mm vs consensus est $301mm. FY27 guide: EPS $2.50-2.70 vs consensus est $2.64, revenue $13.8-14.05bn vs consensus est $14.05bn, EBITDA $1.135-1.175bn vs consensus est $1.16bn, FCF at least $600mm.

J Q4 reported 11/23: EPS $2.20 vs consensus est $2.12, revenue $2.59bn vs consensus est $2.55bn, EBITDA $421mm vs consensus est $413mm, backlog $28.7bn up 24% YoY, book to bill 1.1x. FY27 guide: EPS $8.05-8.45 vs consensus est $8.26, revenue $10-10.35bn vs consensus est $10.12bn, EBITDA margin 15.4-15.7%, FCF margin 8.5-9.5%.

SYM Q4 reported 11/23: EBITDA $114mm vs consensus est $104mm, revenue $778mm vs consensus est $774mm, gross margin 24.8% vs consensus est 24.9%. Q1 guide: EBITDA $110-120mm vs consensus est $109mm, revenue $805-825mm vs consensus est $822mm.
TITN reported better Q3 EPS on topline and gross margins. Fiscal January 2027 guide: agriculture down 10-15% (prior down 15-20%), construction up 2.5-7.5% (prior up 5-10%).
DY and TITN report pre-market 11/24, DE reports pre-market 11/25.
